# Know the Audit Criteria of Quality Assurance Certification. Know the Audit Criteria of Quality Assurance Certification. If you have created a quality management system (QMS) for your business considering the requirements of the top-quality assurance certification, ISO 9001, the next step is to get prepared for the certification audit. What should you do to fulfill the audit criteria of the quality assurance certification? The certification audit is a process when experienced auditors from a third-party certification body will review your QMS, processes, documented records, and employees’ roles to ensure that everything works according to the ISO 9001 requirements. If the auditors find any noncompliance issue anywhere, they will provide suggestions/corrective actions and you need to execute in order to finally be eligible for the ISO 9001 certification. ## Criteria for Passing Audit of the ISO 9001 Quality Assurance Certification. Read more:10 Things Your Quality Assurance Consultant Agency Must Tell You. Our experienced ISO consultants make the internationally accepted management systems implementation journey effortless. An important criterion for ensuring your quality assurance certification is consistency in the processes of your organization. Apart from personally reviewing your processes and documentation, the auditors are also going to enquire whether your organization has done its individual part in making your QMS compliant with the ISO 9001 requirements. If the auditors ever uncover after reviewing your internal audit reports that a problem in your QMS has emerged often but you have not got it resolved, your certification can be at stake. The last key criterion for becoming eligible for ISO certification and passing the audit is a plan for continual improvement of the QMS. Passing the external certification audit is the last but the key step needed for successful **ISO 9001 certification**. These are the intrinsic audit criteria of quality assurance certification and you should not fail at any one of them. Title: Audit & Assurance update: Why do I need an audit? | Hazlewoods: Business Advisers and Accountants
# Audit & Assurance update: Why do I need an audit? Audits play a crucial role in the financial health and transparency of companies. This article explores the importance of audits, the current and upcoming audit thresholds in the UK, and the various benefits audits provide beyond compliance. An audit is an independent examination of financial statements and related records of a company to ensure accuracy and compliance with accounting standards and regulations. The primary goal of an audit is to provide an unbiased opinion on whether the financial statements present a true and fair view of the company’s financial position and performance. In the UK, companies are required by law to have their financial statements audited if they exceed certain thresholds. As of now, a company must have an audit if it meets two out of the following three criteria:. For example, if a UK entity does not breach two of the above thresholds, but is a member of a large global group, an audit will still be required in the UK. **Beyond Compliance: The Strategic Benefits of Audits**. While meeting legal requirements is a primary reason for audits, there are several other compelling reasons why companies should consider regular audits:. While audits are a legal necessity for many companies, their benefits extend far beyond mere compliance. As the audit thresholds in the UK increase from April 2025, companies should carefully consider the strategic advantages of continuing with regular audits, even if they fall below the new thresholds. By embracing audits as a tool for improvement and growth, companies can not only ensure compliance but also build a stronger, more resilient business. ### Does your UK subsidiary need an audit? ### Audit & Assurance update: The benefits of an external audit of your financial statements. ### Audit & Assurance update: New size thresholds for companies and groups. ### Audit & Assurance update: Are you prepared for FRS 102 changes? results.content: Generally, companies are required to have their accounts audited if they exceed specified thresholds related to turnover, assets, and number of employees. To help determine whether your business requires an audit for its first accounting period, we’ve put together a checklist of the key criteria and thresholds. For a first financial year, your company must have its accounts audited if it meets two or more of the following current\* criteria:. These thresholds apply to most private limited companies, for longstanding businesses, the company would enter into the audit threshold if it exceeds the above criteria for the second consecutive year. * **Parent and subsidiary companies**: If the company is part of a group, the group as a whole must meet the thresholds to be exempt from an audit. * **Charities**: Charitable companies have different thresholds and requirements, often needing an audit if their income exceeds £1 million or if they meet certain asset and income condition.
